courses.title: Introduction to International Relations and Diplomacy
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with the analytical skills and critical knowledge to understand key concepts, principles and cases relating to international relations (IR) and diplomatic affairs. Students will be introduced to different kinds of literature, to make them familiar with the actors, goals, means, and consequences of state interaction in the field of international relations. This course will also explore a number of theoretical debates in diplomatic studies, and the practice of global diplomacy with a particular focus on its applicability in the contemporary world order.

courses.subject: DIPL
courses.title: Introduction to International Conflicts and Sanctions
courses.description: This course aims to teach the causes and consequences of international conflicts among nations. In particular, economic sanctions are one of the most popular mechanisms that are used to respond to security challenges. The course will begin with a foundational review of international conflicts and wars. The second part will examine how sanctions are designed and managed as a foreign policy tool. This course will provide an introduction to key debates and practices of policies on international sanctions and discuss the concept and evolution of international sanctions and their role in international conflicts.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to

1. critically analyze the basic forces that shape international conflicts;
2. be familiar with the formulation of sanction policies; and
3. analyze different theories and arguments in the sphere of economic sanctions.
